notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/oelemento__star-sim --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); G1 to G9 passed with no findings. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run. The package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, model_id claude-opus-5-5) and unreviewed (reviewed_by null); no human reviewed or tested it and no hardware or upstream simulator run is claimed. It was written with the new PyLabRobotDriver helper as the structural exemplar of the pylabrobot family.

SHAPE: a config-only PyLabRobotDriver (profile plr-liquid-handler-v1) over the card's entry class star_sim.env:RobotEnv, whose PyLabRobot LiquidHandler is at RobotEnv.lh (star_sim/env.py:60-63). Mode simulated as the card says; risk R2 above the card floor R1 because pipetting is R2 in the MHS-004 hazard table. The upstream can drive a physical STAR (use_hardware=True, star_sim/lab.py:40-43); this package never exposes it and its fake refuses use_hardware.

COVERED: x-cap.oelemento.transfer.v1 and x-cap.oelemento.mix.v1 (self-contained like the upstream primitives: fresh tips from tip tracking, aspirate, dispense, discard; star_sim/primitives.py:55-66, 128-140), x-cap.oelemento.tracked_volumes.v1 (PyLabRobot volume-tracker bookkeeping, star_sim/env.py:113) and the read tips_remaining_columns (TipManager.remaining, star_sim/tip_manager.py:33-42). The per-channel volume is 1 to 1000 uL, cited per operation at the agent tool that performs it (column_transfer agent.py:53, mix_column agent.py:96), and the mix cycles 1 to 10 (agent.py:97); they bound the simulated twin's tool inputs, not a physical STAR. One call uses one column with strictly increasing rows and no repeated well.

SAFETY: no native stop (simulated; PyLabRobot stop() is teardown). An e-stop latches the runtime and the helper sends no further PyLabRobot step of a running operation; the step in progress is not interrupted, so an e-stop during an operation is reported SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED. A step error other than a PyLabRobot bookkeeping error is an unknown outcome and fences the device; with no native stop only a restart of the endpoint recovers it. A failed or interrupted operation performs no cleanup, unlike the upstream primitives, which discard the tips in a finally block (star_sim/primitives.py:65-66): the tips stay mounted and the next operation fails channel_free until the endpoint is restarted.

NOT COVERED: the upstream composite tools column_transfer, multi_dispense and serial_transfer (transfer covers the same PyLabRobot sequence per call), propose_prime and the PlateMap compound/cell records, RobotEnv.reset and observe as a whole, the browser visualizer, flow rates, offsets, liquid heights and blow-out air. The package selects tips itself from tip tracking and never calls TipManager.next_column, so the TipManager cursor behind tips_remaining_columns is not advanced. The fake models PyLabRobot's tip and volume bookkeeping only (no geometry, channel spacing or motion); its capacities and the liquid it seeds into every source well are placeholders (the upstream deck starts empty and is primed by propose_prime, agent.py:825-833). The fake was not compared with the upstream twin: PyLabRobot was not installed where the gate ran, and no sim backend is declared.

Revised on 2026-11-05 after the different-model review (Claude Sonnet, findings A1-A3 and helper findings H1-H8): the mix volume now cites its own tool line, the fidelity gaps name the missing failure cleanup, the package's own tip selection and the one-column rule, safe_state states that the step in progress is not interrupted, and the observe fact names _plate_state. reviewed_by stays null.
